pages.title: Meeting a colleague

situation.text: It is your first week at a new job in the United States. A colleague comes to say hello. You say what you do and exchange business cards.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can greet a new colleague, say what area you work in, ask about their role and exchange a business card.
canDo: Say your area: I work in…
Ask the role: What’s your role?
success: I exchange a card or contact.
pages.think: How do you introduce yourself at a new job? Do you use first names or titles?

teach.goal: Abrir pela situação real: o primeiro contato com um colega novo.
solo: Pergunte como foi (ou será) conhecer colegas no primeiro emprego.
Mostre os 4 critérios.
group: Cada estudante diz uma profissão em inglês.
extra: What job would you like to have?
Who is your favorite coworker?
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.group: One question per student, then a question back to a classmate.

pages.recall: Emails and phone at work (last lesson): “This is Amy from…”. Ask: How do you say your name on the phone?

qs.q: Do you have a business card?

teach.goal: Entrar no idioma e levantar vocabulário de profissões.
extra: What is your job title?

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Names and titles have habits at work. Look at the cards and guess before you read.

cards.note: In many US offices people use first names, even with managers.
In the US they are exchanged simply, often at meetings or events.
In Japan cards are exchanged formally, usually with both hands and with a small bow.

qs.q: What do you call a colleague?

levels.A2: By first name. “Mr.” and “Ms.” are for formal talk.
levels.B1: In many US offices people use first names; with clients you may use Mr. or Ms. first.
levels.B2: First names are the norm in many workplaces, but with customers or in formal fields people start with a title.

levels.A2: A title for a woman, married or not.
levels.B1: “Ms.” is a neutral title for a woman, whatever her marital status.
levels.B2: “Ms.” is the standard neutral title for women in business: it does not show marital status.

qs.q: How do you ask about someone’s job?
qs.pt: Como perguntar sobre o trabalho de alguém?

levels.A2: What do you do? / What’s your role?
levels.B1: You can ask “What’s your role?” or “What do you do here?”
levels.B2: “What’s your role on the team?” is a friendly way to ask what someone is responsible for.

pages.compare: In Brazil people often use “senhor/senhora” or “doutor” early on. In many US offices first names come quickly. What do you do where you live?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto: nomes, títulos e cartões de visita.
solo: Mostre os cartões e peça hipóteses.
Compare com a experiência do estudante.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica.
answers: Q2: a neutral title for a woman.
Q3: What do you do? / What’s your role?
extra: What title is common where you work?
Do you like first names at work?
support: Use as respostas A1 como andaime.
stretch: B2: discuta cuidados ao generalizar: normas variam por empresa e setor.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: Meet has a long /i/ sound; it is a short, relaxed /ɪ/ in “mit” or “sit”. In Portuguese we have only one “i”: practice the difference.

own.criteria: Say it twice. Is “meet” long and “sit” short?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: /i/ longo × /ɪ/ curto (meet × sit).
solo: Modele com o sorriso para /i/ e boca relaxada para /ɪ/.
Identify e depois uso próprio.

pages.title: Group mission — your first week
pages.goal: Each group must meet new colleagues, say what they do and exchange contacts.

missions.mission: Introduce yourselves. Say your areas and roles.
missions.constraint: Use “I work in…” and “What’s your role?”

missions.mission: Introduce yourselves to a manager and ask how to pronounce her name.
missions.constraint: Use “How do you pronounce…?” and “I just started.”

missions.mission: Exchange cards and invite each other to lunch.
missions.constraint: Use “Here’s my card.” and “Let’s have lunch.”

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: conhecer colegas e trocar contatos.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão.
Progressão: com apoio → palavras-chave → sem roteiro.
answers: Modelo: “Nice to meet you!” → “I work in sales. What’s your role?” → “I’m a designer. Here’s my card.”
extra: What if you forget the name?
support: Dê o início de frase em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to introduce yourself to your new team. Say your name, your area and your role.
pages.model: Hi team! I’m Hugo. **I just started** this week. **I work in** sales, and I’m the new assistant. Nice to meet you all! Let’s have lunch soon.
checklist: I said my name and area.
I closed in a friendly way.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos.
group: Troquem os textos e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add one thing you like about the new job.
support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Say your name and area with words.

ladder.say: Nice to meet you. I work in sales. What’s your role?
I just started in sales, so I’m still learning the team.
I joined the sales team last week, and I’m looking forward to working with marketing.
I’d love to hear how marketing and sales could collaborate more closely on upcoming campaigns.
I’d be delighted to explore where our teams’ efforts might usefully converge in the coming quarter.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
